record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: How far do the analogies between relaxor ferroelectrics and manganites go: can relaxor ferroelectrics show colossal responses, do they involve competition between two or more phases, and can chemical composition be tuned to produce phase diagrams as rich as those of manganites, including regimes with long-range order?

evidence.quote: These analogies between ferroelectrics and Mn-oxides should be explored further. For example, is there some sort of "colossal" effect in the relaxor ferroelectrics? Are there two or more phases in competition? Can we alter the chemical compositions and obtain phase diagrams as rich as in manganites, including regimes with long-range order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Relaxor ferroelectrics are disordered dielectric compounds (such as Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-based perovskites) that exhibit a broad, frequency-dependent dielectric response and are believed to contain nanoscale polar regions embedded in a non-polar matrix. Manganites of the form R1-xAxMnO3 (R a rare earth, A a divalent alkaline-earth cation) display colossal magnetoresistance and a rich phase diagram in which ferromagnetic-metallic, charge/orbital-ordered insulating, antiferromagnetic, and inhomogeneous mixed-phase regimes compete as a function of doping x, temperature, and applied fields.

Investigate the following questions concerning the parallels between these two families of materials:

(a) Do relaxor ferroelectrics admit a "colossal" susceptibility analogous to colossal magnetoresistance, in the sense of a giant response of an order-parameter-related observable (e.g., dielectric permittivity, electrostriction, or polarization) to a small external perturbation, induced by the proximity of competing phases?

(b) Can the relaxor state be described as arising from the competition of two or more thermodynamic phases (e.g., a ferroelectric long-range-ordered phase and a non-polar or differently ordered phase), in analogy with the ferromagnetic-metallic vs. charge-ordered insulating competition in manganites?

(c) Can the chemical composition of relaxor ferroelectric solid solutions be tuned so as to produce phase diagrams as rich as those of the manganites, in particular containing well-defined regimes of long-range ferroelectric order separated from relaxor regimes by phase boundaries analogous to the metal–insulator and ferromagnet–charge-ordered boundaries of manganites?

Provide a quantitative or model-based theory addressing (a)–(c), and identify specific compounds and composition ranges in which the predicted analogies can be experimentally tested.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on the analogies between relaxor ferroelectrics and CMR manganites. Phase-competition and nanoscale-inhomogeneity pictures (polar nanoregions, ferroelectric clusters in a paraelectric matrix) are now widely accepted, and "colossal" couplings (e.g., colossal magnetocapacitance in CdCr2S4, giant electromechanical response controlled by polar nanoregion vibrations) have been documented. Theoretical frameworks attributing relaxor behavior to geometric frustration and competing-phase scenarios exist. However, a complete unified theory yielding manganite-like phase diagrams with sharp long-range-order regimes for arbitrary relaxor solid solutions is not established, so the broader programme remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Relaxor ferroelectricity and colossal magnetocapacitive coupling in ferromagnetic CdCr2S4
status_evidence.snippet: Reports relaxor ferroelectricity coexisting with ferromagnetism and a colossal magnetocapacitive effect, exemplifying a colossal response in a relaxor system.
status_evidence.claim: A colossal-type response analogous to those in manganites has been observed in a relaxor ferroelectric.

status_evidence.title: Giant electromechanical coupling of relaxor ferroelectrics controlled by polar nanoregion vibrations
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates that giant electromechanical responses in relaxor ferroelectrics arise from polar nanoregion dynamics, supporting a phase-competition / inhomogeneity picture.
status_evidence.claim: Giant (colossal-like) functional responses in relaxors are linked to competing nanoscale phases.

status_evidence.title: Theory of relaxor-ferroelectricity
status_evidence.snippet: Attributes relaxor properties to geometric frustration impeding long-range ferroelectric order, paralleling phase-competition mechanisms in manganites.
status_evidence.claim: A theoretical mechanism for relaxor behavior in terms of frustrated competing orders has been proposed but is not yet a complete unified theory.

status_evidence.title: Relaxor behavior in manganites (invited)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses relaxor-like behavior directly within manganite systems, reinforcing the cross-family analogy.
status_evidence.claim: Relaxor phenomenology has been identified within manganites themselves.
